post.description:
Sends go over HTTP, not the socket.

The socket is a delivery channel, not the write path: this way every send has
a real status code and natural retry semantics, and the app degrades to
polling rather than breaking when the connection drops.

post.summary: Upload a file, to be attached to a message
post.description:
Upload first, send second.

Decoupling the two means a large file uploads while the person is still
typing, and a failed send does not lose the upload.

get.description:
Serve a stored file.

The path is resolved through the storage backend, which refuses any key that
escapes the upload root — the key arrives from a URL, so traversal is checked
rather than assumed.

AttachmentRead.title: AttachmentRead
AttachmentRead.description: A file carried by a message. URLs are built from the opaque storage key.

ChallengeResponse.title: ChallengeResponse
ChallengeResponse.description:
Acknowledges that a verification code has been issued.

``dev_code`` is populated only outside production. Verification is mocked by
design (see the brief), and surfacing the code here is what lets a reviewer
complete the flow without an SMS provider. The production branch omits it, so
the mock cannot silently become a live vulnerability.

identifier.title: Identifier
identifier.description: A phone number in international format, or a username.

ContactCreate.title: ContactCreate
ContactCreate.description: Add someone by whichever identifier the person happens to know.

ContactRead.title: ContactRead
ContactRead.description: A saved contact, with the underlying account attached.

ConversationRead.title: ConversationRead
ConversationRead.description: A conversation as it appears in the list or the chat header.

ConversationType.title: ConversationType
ConversationType.description: A conversation is either between exactly two people, or a named group.

ConversationUpdate.title: ConversationUpdate
ConversationUpdate.description: Change group metadata, or the shared disappearing-message timer.

LastMessagePreview.title: LastMessagePreview
LastMessagePreview.description:
The one-line summary shown against a conversation in the list.

Content is decrypted and truncated server-side. Sending the whole message
just to render 40 characters would waste bandwidth on every conversation in
the list, on every load.

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest
LoginRequest.description: Request a fresh verification code for an existing account.

MessageRead.title: MessageRead
MessageRead.description: A message as the client renders it.

MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse
MessageResponse.description: Trivial acknowledgement for endpoints with nothing meaningful to return.

MessageStatus.title: MessageStatus
MessageStatus.description:
Delivery lifecycle as presented in the UI.

Derived from receipt rows rather than stored on the message: in a group the
same message is simultaneously read by one member and merely delivered to
another, so a single column could not represent the truth. ``SENDING`` is
client-side only — it describes a message the server has not yet acknowledged.

MessageType.title: MessageType
MessageType.description:
What a message row represents.

``SYSTEM`` covers events the transcript should show but no user typed —
someone joined, the group was renamed, the disappearing timer changed.
Modelling them as messages keeps the timeline a single ordered sequence
instead of forcing the client to merge two streams.

ParticipantRead.title: ParticipantRead
ParticipantRead.description: A member of a conversation, with their role and membership state.

ParticipantRole.title: ParticipantRole
ParticipantRole.description: Group authority. Direct conversations treat everyone as a member.

QuotedMessage.title: QuotedMessage
QuotedMessage.description:
The compact form of a message being replied to.

A snapshot rather than a nested MessageRead: replies would otherwise nest
recursively down a long chain, and a quote only ever renders one line.

ReactionSummary.title: ReactionSummary
ReactionSummary.description:
Reactions of one emoji, aggregated for display.

Sending every individual reaction row would make a popular message expensive
to render; the client needs the emoji, the count, who reacted, and whether
the viewer is among them.

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description: Optional body for refresh, when no cookie is available.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest
RegisterRequest.description: Start registration for a new phone number.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
A newly issued session.

The refresh token is also set as an httpOnly cookie. It is returned in the
body as well so that non-browser clients and the test suite can drive the
flow without cookie handling — a browser should prefer the cookie, which
JavaScript cannot read and therefore cannot leak through XSS.

UserPrivate.title: UserPrivate
UserPrivate.description: Your own account, which does include the identifying phone number.

UserPublic.title: UserPublic
UserPublic.description:
Another person as they appear to you.

Deliberately excludes phone_number: it is the login identifier, and exposing
every participant's number to everyone in a group would leak personal contact
details that Signal treats as private.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: Editable profile fields. Every field optional — this is a partial update.

VerifyRequest.title: VerifyRequest
